reason: MECHANISM: in the mutant the condition still reads the real m['within'] (int? true for a responds_within monitor), but the value is read from m[''], which a monitor never has, so ival(nil) is nil and w = nil; `(1..w)` is then the endless range (1..nil) and `.map { |i| "pending:#{i}" }` appends one fresh String per iteration with no bound, so memory grows until the address-space cap and the process spends its whole limit in allocation retries (no test can complete the call). UNMUTATED: for an Integer within, (1..w) is finite (w <= 2**53-1 is bounded by int?, and the monitors under test use w <= 3), so the same tests finish in milliseconds under the same limits. `racy`: where the allocation failure reaches a test first the mutant is an ordinary kill, which the merge then requires to be plainly killed in that run.

MECHANISM: that statement is the only advance of the cursor o in `while o < rec_end` (the measurement-block loop). Deleted, o keeps its value 8 (or the previous block's start) after every block, so `o < rec_end` stays true, the same block is parsed again and `measurements << {...}` appends a fresh Hash with a fresh digest String each time: an unbounded loop that grows a live array until memory is exhausted (the raise checks inside the loop pass because the same bytes are valid each time), so no test completes the call. UNMUTATED: o advances by 4 + size >= 7 per block and the loop ends at rec_end, so the same tests finish in milliseconds. `racy`: where a test-level deadline or allocation failure reaches a test first the mutant is an ordinary kill, which the merge then requires to be plainly killed in that run.
